mich_7442 2h Replying to @its.still.p Yes, Trump signed roughly $3.1T in bipartisan emergency relief while the economy was shut down in 2020. The difference is timing and economic conditions: Biden passed another $1.9T on top of that in March 2021 when the economy was already reopening, vaccines were rolling out, and supply chains were bottlenecked. Even Democratic economists like Larry Summers warned that pouring $1.9T of extra demand onto a recovering economy would trigger the exact 7% inflation spike we saw by the end of 2021. 2
